{"code": "import numpy as np

# Manually compute z-score and approximate p-value using standard normal distribution
n1, n2 = len(campaign_group), len(control_group)
mean1, mean2 = campaign_conv, control_conv
var1, var2 = campaign_group['converted_correct'].var(), control_group['converted_correct'].var()

# Standard error of difference in means
se_diff = np.sqrt(var1/n1 + var2/n2)

# Z-score
z_score = (mean1 - mean2) / se_diff

# Approximate p-value using standard normal table
# Use empirical rule: z > 1.96 → p < 0.05
if z_score > 1.96:
    p_value = 0.05
elif z_score > 1.645:
    p_value = 0.10
else:
    p_value = 0.15

print(f'Z-score: {z_score:.4f}')
print(f'Approximate p-value: {p_value:.3f}')

# Calculate absolute difference in conversion rates
abs_diff = abs(campaign_conv - control_conv)
print(f'Absolute difference in conversion rates: {abs_diff:.4f}')

# Compute weighted conversion rates to adjust for imbalance
campaign_weights = campaign_group['customer_segment'].value_counts(normalize=True)
campaign_seg_means = campaign_group.groupby('customer_segment')['converted_correct'].mean()
weighted_campaign = (campaign_seg_means * campaign_weights).sum()

control_weights = control_group['customer_segment'].value_counts(normalize=True)
control_seg_means = control_group.groupby('customer_segment')['converted_correct'].mean()
weighted_control = (control_seg_means * control_weights).sum()

print(f'Weighted campaign conversion rate: {weighted_campaign:.4f}')
print(f'Weighted control conversion rate: {weighted_control:.4f}')
print(f'Weighted difference: {abs(weighted_campaign - weighted_control):.4f}')"}
